- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to avoid overshoot unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.80) but forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates upside; adjust upward by 1–2% if sentiment persists.
- Model frequently overestimates mean price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.5–0.77); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to align with true mean reversion.
- When sentiment turns negative (0.00–0.27) mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; if sentiment drops below 0.27 after day 10, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing filter to first 5 days of forecast to reduce noise.
